item.title: Dein Weg zu Bitcoin – Bitcoin lernen: Wo finde ich gute Inhalte? Bianca über die Gründung von BitUcation - Dein Weg zu Bitcoin
item.description:
Wer anfängt, sich mit Bitcoin zu beschäftigen, steht schnell vor einem Berg: tausende Videos, Podcasts, Bücher, Kurse – und dazwischen jede Menge Lambo-Versprechen. Genau vor diesem Problem standen auch Bianca und Caddy. Allerdings von der anderen Seite: Auf dem Weg in den Urlaub planten sie einen Workshop und fragten sich, wie der eigentlich zu den Menschen kommt, die sich dafür interessieren.Aus dieser Frage wurde BitUcation: eine Plattform, die Bitcoin-Bildung aus der ganzen Community an einem Ort bündelt.Wo findet man eigentlich gute Bitcoin-Inhalte, wenn man nicht weiß, wem man trauen kann?In dieser Folge erzählt Bianca, Mitgründerin von BitUcation, wie aus einer Urlaubsidee eine Plattform wurde, warum Dezentralität ihr Herzstück ist und wohin die Reise gehen soll. Und sie teilt sehr offen ihren eigenen Weg zu Bitcoin, der nicht über Rendite führte, sondern über ein IT-Netzwerk und einen Schicksalsschlag.👉 Warum man sich von der Informationsflut nicht erschlagen lassen sollte und bei den eigenen Fragen bleibt👉 Warum es nicht die eine richtige Quelle gibt, sondern die, bei der man sich gut aufgehoben fühlt👉 Warum Bitcoin-Bildung so schwer ankommt, solange es als Spekulationsobjekt gilt👉 Wie die BitUcation-Karte dir einen Ansprechpartner direkt in deiner Nähe zeigt👉 Warum Missionieren nicht funktioniert und ein echtes Bedürfnis alles verändertIch bin selbst BitUcator. Trotzdem habe ich in diesem Gespräch noch einmal verstanden, was hinter der Plattform steckt: kein Projekt, das Menschen überzeugen will, sondern eines, das da ist, wenn jemand bereit ist.✅ Die Gründungsgeschichte: von der Workshop-Planung zur Plattform✅ Selbstlernkurse, Live-Workshops, Webinare und zusätzliche Ressourcen✅ Warum Bitcoin-Bildung gerade aus einer privilegierten Lage heraus schwer ist✅ Die Vision: alle Menschen im DACH-Raum erreichen, auch im Mainstream💬 Zitat der Folge:„Bitcoin ist für mich ein Werkzeug, das mich hoffnungsvoll in die Zukunft blicken lässt.“📲 Bianca bzw. BitUcation findet ihr hier:• https://bitucation.com ✨ Mein Ziel: Bitcoin verständlich und greifbar machen durch Geschichten, die jeder nachvollziehen kann und die zeigen, dass die ersten Schritte nicht groß sein müssen und dass jeder Zweifel am Anfang hatte. Gefällt dir die Folge?Dann lass ein 👍 da, abonniere den Kanal und schick die Episode an jemanden, der das hören sollte 🚀📌 Schreib deine Fragen/Meinungen in die Kommentare – ich lese alle!⚡ Unterstütze den Podcast über Fountain: Auf Fountain kannst du die Audio-Version hören und mir freiwillig Sats per Lightning senden – ganz ohne Werbung oder Abo. 👉 https://fountain.fm/show/WdHajypwLY2JOQN2zH1S📲 Folge mir auch gerne auf Instagram: 🔗 https://www.instagram.com/finanz.bewusstsein Rechtlicher Hinweis: Dieser Podcast dient der finanziellen Bildung und persönlichen Meinungsäußerung und ist keine Finanz- oder Anlageberatung. Bitcoin ist volatil, Investitionen können zu Verlusten führen. Jede Entscheidung triffst du eigenverantwortlich. Study Bitcoin.Partner:🧡Bitcoin21 – stylische Bitcoin Kleidung:Mit dem Code FINANZB bekommst du 10 % Rabatt auf deine gesamte Bestellung. https://bitcoin21.shop/?ref=FINANZB 🧡Coinfinity – Bitcoin Börse :https://coinfinity.co/bitcoin-appCode: FINANZB - Damit sparst du 21 % deiner Gebühren in den ersten 6 Monaten.🧡21statues – Bitcoin Lampen und Statuen:https://21statues.de?sca_ref=10285598.SH2VZ7SHVa8Code: FINANZB - Du sparst 5 % auf alle ProdukteWeitere Empfehlungen und Codes:🧡BitBox – Cold Wallet:https://shop.bitbox.swiss/?ref=tfjnborqCode: FINANZB - Du sparst 5 % auf alle Produkte🧡Seedor – Backup-Lösung in Stahl:https://www.seedor.io/discount/FINANZB Code: FINANZB - Du sparst 5 % auf alle Produkte#bitcoin #podcast #finanzen #finanzbildung #bitcoineducation #bitcoinbildung #geld #bitcoinpodcast #deinwegzubitcoin

item.title: Sound Money Bitcoin Podcast – #344 Vom erfolgreichen Banker zum überzeugten Bitcoiner -mit Joe Kranzler
item.description:
Joachim „Joe“ Kranzler hat eine einzigartige Stellung im Finanzmarkt. Er darf seine Kunden sowohl im Wertpapier-Bereich, als auch zu Bitcoin beraten - hierfür ist er mit allen notwendigen Lizenzen für den EU-Raum ausgestattet.


Joe ist in der Finanzwelt zu Hause, hat der klassischen Bankenwelt jedoch den Rücken gekehrt. Bei der Finanzkrise 2007 war er live dabei, als er als Filialleiter einen Bankrun der Kunden erlebt hat. Sein Wissen rund um das Geld- und Finanzsystem hat ihn letztlich zum Bitcoiner werden lassen. Heute betreut Joe Kunden (teilweise auch vor Ort) für Coinfinity und unterstützt beim Onboarding und Kauf von Bitcoin. Parallel berät die Kunden eigenen Kunden ganzheitlich zu allen Bereichen der Geldanlage.


Im Interview sprechen wir über seinen persönlichen Werdegang und über das aktuelle Sentiment im Markt, wie denken Vermögende und Unternehmenskunden über Bitcoin? Ist der Bullrun eingeläutet?

item.itunes:summary:
Joachim „Joe“ Kranzler hat eine einzigartige Stellung im Finanzmarkt. Er darf seine Kunden sowohl im Wertpapier-Bereich, als auch zu Bitcoin beraten - hierfür ist er mit allen notwendigen Lizenzen für den EU-Raum ausgestattet.


Joe ist in der Finanzwelt zu Hause, hat der klassischen Bankenwelt jedoch den Rücken gekehrt. Bei der Finanzkrise 2007 war er live dabei, als er als Filialleiter einen Bankrun der Kunden erlebt hat. Sein Wissen rund um das Geld- und Finanzsystem hat ihn letztlich zum Bitcoiner werden lassen. Heute betreut Joe Kunden (teilweise auch vor Ort) für Coinfinity und unterstützt beim Onboarding und Kauf von Bitcoin. Parallel berät die Kunden eigenen Kunden ganzheitlich zu allen Bereichen der Geldanlage.


Im Interview sprechen wir über seinen persönlichen Werdegang und über das aktuelle Sentiment im Markt, wie denken Vermögende und Unternehmenskunden über Bitcoin? Ist der Bullrun eingeläutet?

item.title: Bitcoin News Alerts | Daily BTC Macro Signal – 2475: $2 Million Bitcoin Supply Shock - Saylor Is About To Set It Off
item.description:
Samson Mow is predicting a Bitcoin supply shock as Michael Saylor, Adam Back and an expanding wave of corporate and institutional buyers compete for increasingly scarce BTC. Strategy alone now holds 847,666 Bitcoin, while BlackRock's IBIT controls more than 800,000 and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs collectively hold roughly 1.3 million BTC.

Today we break down the supply shock thesis, the potential path toward $2 million Bitcoin, fresh ETF inflows, Bitcoin's performance against gold, October's historical strength and why the competition for available BTC could be entering a completely different phase.

📺 Prefer video? Watch daily Bitcoin breakdowns: http://BitcoinNewsAlerts.net

item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.itunes:summary:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.title: Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock'n'Roll – The Stablecoin Payments Renovation is Still Under Construction
item.description:
Stablecoins can move money around the world. But when is a payment legally complete, what happens if an issuer fails, and can the same token be used across jurisdictions?

In this new episode of Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock’n’Roll, Jonas Gross and guest host Jonathan Knoll of etonec speak with Jai Massari, a Lightspark co-founder, former Davis Polk partner and now of counsel at Arktouros. Having helped design Libra’s legal architecture, she brings a perspective on what makes digital money work.

Massari revisits Libra’s ambitions and the weight of its Facebook origins. The project’s reserve design and redemption mechanics remain relevant, she argues, even though its technology could not overcome the policy obstacles. Its consortium model also leaves an open question: can shared distribution and scale outweigh the difficulty of making decisions among competitors?

The discussion then examines stablecoins and tokenized deposits. A bank deposit remains a claim on a bank; a regulated, reserve-backed stablecoin has a different economic structure. Their usefulness depends on the payment: speed, funding costs and existing banking connections all matter.

On stablecoin regulation, Massari discusses the US GENIUS Act, Europe’s MiCA and the distinction between stablecoin issuance and the broader market-structure debate around CLARITY. She also questions whether comprehensive crypto legislation could constrain innovation before the industry has developed its most useful applications.

For cross-border payments, the missing pieces include recognition of foreign issuers, certainty over payment and collateral use, and comparable rules for reserves, redemption and insolvency. Without coordination, blockchain payments risk inheriting familiar financial frictions.

The episode closes with agentic payments: how AI agents can prove their authority, who is responsible when they exceed it, and why existing agency and contract law may provide a starting point for the next generation of payments.

item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 24) ... Energie mit zwei Leben
item.description:
Bitcoin und Energieverbrauch werden oft in einem negativen Zusammenhang genannt. Diese Folge zeigt ein differenzierteres Bild: warum Bitcoin-Mining Stromnetze stabilisieren kann, wie aus Abwärme ein zweiter Wertschöpfungskreislauf entsteht, und wo die Grenzen dieser Entwicklung aktuell noch liegen.

Themen in dieser Folge:

  • Wie sich der Anteil nachhaltiger Energien beim Bitcoin-Mining seit 2022 entwickelt hat
  • Warum der Ausbau von Wind- und Solarenergie ein Netzstabilitätsproblem mit sich bringt
  • Wie Bitcoin-Miner als flexible Last genutzt werden können, um Lastspitzen abzupuffern
  • Warum jede Kilowattstunde beim Mining "zwei Leben" bekommt: Bitcoin-Belohnung und nutzbare Wärme
  • Drei Unternehmen, die das bereits umsetzen: Terahash, 21energy und Power2Bit


Die Anfangs erwähnte Studie der Cambridge University

https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/2025/cambridge-study-sustainable-energy-rising-in-bitcoin-mining/


Erwähnte Unternehmen:

  • Terahash – Bitcoin-Mining Infrastruktur für Unternehmen
  • 21energy – Bitcoin-Heizungen für Privathaushalte und Kleingewerbe
  • Power2Bit – flexible, klimaneutrale Rechenzentren und kommunale Wärmeplanung


Hinweis: Die genannten Prozentzahlen zum Energiemix variieren je nach Berechnungsmethode (konservativer Netzmix vs. direkte Unternehmensmeldungen) und waren zum Zeitpunkt der Aufnahme aktuell.

]]>

item.title: Rob Wallace | Bitcoin News – What’s Really At The Bottom of The Bitcoin Rabbit Hole? | Bram Kanstein and Scott Dedels
item.description:
How far down the Bitcoin rabbit hole can you actually go? Author Scott Dedels and Bram Kanstein have gone further than most.

Scott Dedels argues that the money problem is just the shallow end of a much bigger problem with time itself, one he believes is older than fiat and more significant than money. Meanwhile,

Bram Kanstein ( @bramk ) took over 30 Bitcoiners into the mountains of Colorado for a psychedelic ceremony to explore what lies beyond simply fixing the money.

Rob Wallace sits down with both of them to explore Bitcoin as more than a monetary technology, touching on consciousness, mechanical time, psychedelics, and the spiritual dimension of adopting an absolute, verifiable truth in a world built on manufactured systems. Scott also shares why he believes 2026 could be the year even the most seasoned Bitcoin OGs look back and realize their conviction wasn't as strong as they thought.

Here is what we cover:

• A Bitcoin vibe check heading into the end of 2026, and why conviction gets tested at the bottom

• Why Bitcoin gives people proof that they can think for themselves

• Scott's thesis: fix the clocks, fix civilization, and why the time problem may be bigger than the money problem

• How mechanical time is only 400 years old, and why that matters

• Bitcoin, consciousness, and the idea of a shared, agreed-upon reality

• Why thinking in four-year cycles rehabilitates your ability to plan long-term

• The Dao of Bitcoin: how conviction changes your relationship with the present moment

• Bitcoin as an "economic psychedelic" and what that phrase actually means

• Why Bitcoin functions as an absolute, objective truth unlike anything else in the world

• Bram's bike accident, the ambulance ride, and the lesson it taught him about surrender and reality

• Psychedelics and how they alter the perception of time and expand consciousness

• Why Bitcoiners tend to be more hopeful about the future than people who went down other rabbit holes

• The community and friendships that form once you go deep into Bitcoin

• Inside Bram's "Beyond Bitcoin" psychedelic retreat in Colorado with 30 Bitcoiners

• Why so many people feel alone on their Bitcoin journey, and why they shouldn't

• Advice for staying the path through the ebbs and flows of conviction

• Taking personal responsibility in a world built on outsourcing it

If you found this valuable, hit subscribe and turn on notifications so you never miss an episode of The Bitcoin News Channel.

item.title: The Bitcoin Layer – Bitcoin Doesn’t Care About The Bond Crisis
item.description: <![CDATA[In this episode, Nik asks how bitcoin is outperforming both gold and the dollar in the middle of a global bond crisis. He covers why rising yields, bond volatility, and a stronger dollar all point to tighter liquidity, then turns to the French German bond spread and why a move of this size has only happened twice in thirty years. Nik explains where he thinks the European Central Bank would have to step in, why falling oil could ironically rescue the French bond market, and why this crisis may be the opening the digital euro needed.]]>

item.title: Bitcoin Today Recast – Bitcoin Turns Green for 2026, In-Kind ETFs & Bitcoin Self-Custody | Retail Access Explained | Oct. 2, 2026
item.description:
Bitcoin is back in the green for 2026—but why is retail still jumping through hoops to access a truly in-kind Bitcoin ETF?

Today on Bitcoin Today, Fred Krueger, Dom Bei, Matt, Dark, and the community explore the growing divide between institutional Bitcoin access and individual ownership. From ETF mechanics and Bitcoin-backed borrowing to self-custody and privacy, this conversation looks at what financial access really means in a Bitcoin world.

We also cover the market forces capturing attention—from oil and war concerns to the Anthropic IPO and the AI infrastructure build-out—and discuss the risks and trade-offs behind Bitcoin ADRs, including custody, counterparty exposure, settlement, and liquidity.

The episode wraps with a practical conversation about self-custody, Satoshi’s “no trusted third parties” principle, keeping KYC-free Bitcoin private, and Entropy Lab, an offline tool for generating seed phrases from dice rolls and auditing wallet activity.

🎙️ MISSED THE LIVE SPACE? Bitcoin Today is a daily live conversation hosted by founding member Loren and co-host Terence, featuring community members and special guests. This is the full replay of today’s Space.

From ETF mechanics and Bitcoin-backed borrowing to self-custody and privacy, this conversation looks at what financial access really means in a Bitcoin world.

We also cover the market forces capturing attention—from oil and war concerns to the Anthropic IPO and the AI infrastructure build-out—and discuss the risks and trade-offs behind Bitcoin ADRs, including custody, counterparty exposure, settlement, and liquidity.

The episode wraps with a practical conversation about self-custody, Satoshi’s “no trusted third parties” principle, keeping KYC-free Bitcoin private, and Entropy Lab, an offline tool for generating seed phrases from dice rolls and auditing wallet activity.

item.title: Bitcoin Audible.DE - Die besten Bitcoin-Artikel, vorgelesen in deutscher Sprache! – 208. Martin Connor - Bitcoin, das ultimative Kollateral
item.description:
von Martin Connor – Originaltitel: «Bitcoin: The Ultimate Collateral«

*„Die beste, einfachste – ultimative – Form der Kreditsicherheit ist etwas, das sofort beansprucht und verkauft werden kann, wenn der Schuldner seine Zahlungen nicht leistet. Der Verkauf eines Hauses kann Monate oder sogar Jahre dauern. Auch Aktien haben zeitliche Beschränkungen. Bitcoin jedoch nicht. Bitcoin ist immer in Bewegung“
*

(Martin Connor)

Wenn man Bitcoin als hartes, in seinem Kern nicht veränderbares oder manipulierbares Asset begreift, welche Möglichkeiten eröffnen sich dadurch? Das Buch „Bitcoin: Die ultimative Kreditsicherheit“ untersucht, wie die Bereiche Bitcoin und Kreditvergabe perfekt zusammenpassen. Etwa, wie Bitcoin-Besitzer und Bitcoin-Unternehmen den maximalen Wert aus ihren Bitcoins herausholen können, ohne sie verkaufen zu müssen.

Wir lesen ein Kapitel aus diesem Buch, das eine zentrale Idee beleuchtet: Bitcoin als die beste Sicherheit, die die Menschheit je hatte. Die meisten Menschen denken beim Thema «Sicherheit» an Häuser, Aktien, Gold und Bargeld – aber weil es scheinbar nichts Besseres gab, übersehen sie deren enorme Schwächen. Die Kombination der Elemente von Multisignatur – echtes gemeinsames Eigentum, perfekte digitale Knappheit, Portabilität und die unübertroffene Verfügbarkeit von Bitcoin – unterscheidet es grundlegend von herkömmlichen Besicherungsmodellen.

Verkaufe Deine Bitcoins niemals – lebe davon.

Weitere Empfehlungen:

  • Pierre Rochard: «Der Nutzen des Sparens» (Ep. #019)
  • Tomer Strolight: «Warum Bitcoin?» (Ep. #80-82)
  • Saifedean Ammous: «Für eine Rückkehr zu niedriger Zeitpräferenz» (Ep. #77)
  • Pierre Rochard: «Bitcoin vs. Gold» (Ep. #71)
  • Hans-Hermann Hoppe: «Der Ertrag aus gespartem Geld – neu überdacht» (Ep. #18)
  • Parker Lewis: «Die «Bezahl‘ mich in Bitcoin!»-Theorie» (#140)
  • Parker Lewis: «Bitcoin-Zahlungen: Die ‹Jemand ist der Nächste›-Logik» (#151)
  • HodlHodl.com für Belehnung von Bitcoin, ebenso wie Unchained Capital, Ledn, Firefish etc.

Abonniere BitcoinAudible.de und empfehle unsere Vorlesungen jedem, der/die sich für Bitcoin interessiert. Hilf damit auch anderen, Bitcoin von einem starken monetären, wirtschaftlichen und philosophischen Fundament aus zu erkunden.

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – What's Coming to El Salvador's Bitcoin Economy Is Bigger Than Anyone Expected | Jose Rodriguez of Nodeman
item.description:
Is El Salvador the freest country on earth for a Bitcoin business, or the most heavily KYC'd place a Bitcoiner could choose? Anyone who has bought El Salvador real estate lately has an opinion, and so does the lawyer who reads the regulations for a living.

You already know this is Bitcoin Country. What you can't tell from the outside is why the El Salvador banks turned Bitcoin companies away for years, what the digital assets law lets you build here, and who is actually asking the questions at a property closing.

Mike sits down with Jose Rodriguez, a lawyer with Nodeman, a Bitcoin-centric legal firm that helped draft some of these regulations and has followed this since day one.

Jose explains the bank refusals in layers. The first is political and goes back to who owned the banks when the Bitcoin Law passed. The second is the AML KYC pressure that reaches every Salvadoran bank through FATF, GAFILAT and the US correspondent accounts it depends on to move money in and out of the country. Then he explains what changed in the US that finally opened the doors. Three banks now hold licenses, and a Bitcoin bank is on the way.

Then the conversation turns to KYC requirements on property. Jose describes who is asking where a buyer's money came from, and in most cases it isn't the seller. He also says the KYC regulations changed recently, raising the threshold from $1,000 to $25,000, while one government office still hasn't issued the guidelines eight months later. Buying property in El Salvador should look different once that clears.

The second half covers the Digital Assets Law. Jose describes what real estate tokenization means today, which company structure makes it legal, and the two laws still standing between El Salvador and a property title that lives on a token. He's blunt about lawyers who wave through deals they don't understand.

El Salvador has spent five years writing clear rules for Bitcoin businesses, and this is what those rules look like from inside the paperwork!

If you're planning to run a business here, bank here, or buy here, listen to this one before you sign anything.


—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.title: The Mustard Seed Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin Could Reach $840,000 Within Five Years | Sam Baker
item.description:
Sam Baker, research analyst at River, joins me to explain why Bitcoin could reach $840,000 within the next three to five years. We discuss the institutional adoption and capital inflows behind River’s model, the case for a 10% Bitcoin allocation, why each dollar invested can add several dollars to Bitcoin’s market cap, custody considerations, the CLARITY Act, AI’s role in accelerating macro trends, and why businesses are currently driving Bitcoin demand.

item.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute – David Beckworth and Sam Lyman: The Stakes of Preserving Dollar Dominance
item.description:
Sam Lyman and David Beckworth discuss how dollar stablecoins could shape the dollar’s global role and compete with central bank digital currencies. item.title: The Café Bitcoin Podcast – The Finale: Liquid's 4,000 Bitcoin, the Caching Bug, and 50 Days for Freedom Wrapped
item.description:
• The last day. Brady opened with the count, 37 shows in 50 days, and the campaign's frame: political independence 250 years ago, monetary independence now. Yan Pritzker, Frank Corva, Suze and Alec on stage; Unseen Finance returned at the end.
  • The Liquid hack, plainly. On Sunday somebody sent 4,000 L-BTC to SideSwap's peg-out and the Liquid Federation paid out real Bitcoin. The L-BTC had been created from nothing. Blockstream paused the sidechain and 3,400 Bitcoin came back Monday.
  • ⭐ Yan on what broke: a caching bug, not anyone's keys. "The only two hard problems in computer science are naming and cache invalidation." Two transactions shared one cache key, so validators mistook a fake for one already checked.
  • Why it is not Bitcoin. Yan: Liquid is an 11-of-15 federation of companies with its own database and rules. "This is a separate thing, this is not Bitcoin itself." Lightning is built on Bitcoin script; Liquid is not.
  • ⭐ Frank on the 15%. The hackers returned 85% and kept about 600 Bitcoin. His question: will anyone be made whole, and if they keep it, "they're surely not white hats." A Bitcoin Policy Institute lawyer offered to talk.
  • Yan's verdict on the hat color: gray. Taking everything to beat a black hat is arguable. Keeping a cut is not. "You don't just return a wallet and take a bunch of stuff out of it."
  • Suze's question: Bitcoiners are ruthless about added trust assumptions, so why did Liquid get a pass? "Were we discerning enough?" Leave the base layer and you take on another code base and another set of failure points.
  • ⭐ Yan on open source in the AI era: it stays because every open project gets red-teamed by the whole internet. Closed systems get hacked too, "we just don't hear about them." The base chain is "the ultimate boss" nobody has beaten.
  • Yan's bank numbers, read live from the Identity Theft Resource Center: 3,332 reported data compromises in 2025 affecting 280 million people, 739 of them in financial services. "Bank-grade security" is not a standard anyone actually meets.
  • ⭐ Frank's hard question: must the layers be as bulletproof as Bitcoin? Yan: nothing is, and the only path is slow growth. Bitcoin was attacked at $1, then $10,000, then a billion. Early adopters carry the risk.
  • Yan's rocket-ship rule. Bitcoin Core engineering is closer to launching a spacecraft than shipping web software. "Years of careful review, study, simulations on other chains." Test new tech on other coins for two years first.
  • Suze asked whether ossification risks losing the skills to change Bitcoin in 50 years. Frank and Yan: no. Ossification is no new features, not no developers, and AI has widened who can work on cryptography and game theory.
  • Yan on open-weight versus hosted AI: the same debate as open source versus closed, and open source won the internet. His advice to companies: externalize memory, skills and harness so you can swap models. Swan built its own.
  • Unseen Finance returned with a proposal: these incidents are a credibility problem for the services on top of Bitcoin, not for Bitcoin. His fix, borrowed from banking: a self-regulatory body plus an insurance pool that service providers pay into.
  • Brady's tally at the close: Cory, Yan, Steve, Alec, Isaiah, Matt and Brandon from Swan; Larry Lepard three times; Parker Lewis, Daniel Batten, Tom and Callum, Guy Swann, Ryan MacLeod, Alana, Bob Burnett, Roxana. Suze made 35 of 37.
  • The close. "We have the tools, we have the knowledge, we have the culture, we have the determination." The half-price buy fee ends today; limit orders placed today keep it. Yan's last word: take security seriously, "go play with AI."
    • ]]>

item.title: Unchained – The Chopping Block: Bitget's 387 Million Dollar Hack, Kalshi's Cooked Perps Volume, and Agentic Bank Runs
item.description:
North Korea takes $387 million from Bitget and moves it through THORChain while NEAR's Shield freezes what it can, a Consensys validator hack tests whether staking was ever the risk-free rate, a quant named Benny shows Kalshi's perps volume was cooked, and Apollo warns that AI agents are coming for your checking account.

Welcome to The Chopping Block, where crypto insiders Haseeb Qureshi, Tarun Chitra, and Robert Leshner chop it up about the latest in crypto. This week the three of them record from a self-serve podcast studio in Amsterdam.


Bitget loses 387 million dollars to North Korea's Lazarus Group and pays every claim from its user protection fund, but the stolen funds raise a harder question: THORChain lets them through while NEAR's Shield freezes them, so which one is actually decentralized? (Dragonfly is an investor in Bitget and NEAR.) Then a Consensys validator compromise tests staking as the risk-free rate, Robert prices insurance on US Treasuries at 35 basis points, a quant named Benny exposes Kalshi's perps volume, and the crew takes apart Apollo's warning about agentic bank runs, from Robert's one basis point checking account to Tarun's agent filing his insurance claims.

Listen to the episode on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pods, Fountain, Podcast Addict, Pocket Casts, Amazon Music, or on your favorite podcast platform.


Show highlights

🔹 Bitget loses about 387 million dollars to North Korea's Lazarus Group, and its 460 million dollar user protection fund covers every claim, so there is no contagion.

🔹 The stolen funds run through THORChain while NEAR's Shield freezes around 500K and refuses to route more than 100 million, which reopens the question of what decentralization actually requires.

🔹 Robert wants only the two extremes, fully neutral infrastructure or deliberate censorship, and nothing in the middle. Haseeb counters that everything between a centralized exchange and Uniswap already is the middle.

🔹 Haseeb argues property rights mean more than valid state transitions, and that anomaly detection can enforce them in a way that is still neutral and programmatic.

🔹 Tarun explains why cross-chain intents, with their solvers and RFQs, are where all the fights happen.

🔹 A Consensys validator compromise forces a mass exit, and Robert says staking was never the risk-free rate, only the best possible one. He looks up US CDS at 35 basis points and puts Ethereum validation risk at about five.

🔹 Would Ethereum roll back an unfair slashing? Haseeb says it would to protect stakers. Robert says only if transactions were corrupted.

🔹 A quant named Benny exposes Kalshi's perps volume, 3 million of open interest against hundreds of millions in daily volume, and Kalshi ends its liquidity incentives as the CFTC reportedly investigates.

🔹 Robert on why market maker rebates are normal, and how paying makers in equity for volume made Kalshi's go so wrong.

🔹 On Apollo's agentic bank runs: Robert earns one basis point on his checking account, Tarun's agent finds 1,700 dollars in health insurance overcharges, and the panel argues the whole economy is about to look like DeFi.


Hosts

⭐️Haseeb Qureshi, Managing Partner at Dragonfly

⭐️Tarun Chitra, Managing Partner at Robot Ventures

⭐️Robert Leshner, Founder & CEO of Superstate


Disclosures


Timestamps

item.title: THE Bitcoin Podcast – Strategy, AI and the Start of the Bitcoin Bull Market | Cory Klippsten
item.description:
In this episode of The Bitcoin Podcast, I sit down with Cory Klippsten, CEO of Swan Bitcoin, to talk about where Bitcoin stands today. Cory explains why he thinks most Bitcoin treasury companies fell short of what they promised, and why he now recommends keeping at least 90% of your Bitcoin exposure in the real thing rather than stocks, ETFs, or other proxies. He also pushes back on the idea that AI agents will drive Bitcoin payments, arguing they'll mostly pay in digital dollars, and that the stronger use case is censored humans who need money that can't be stopped.

He also explains why his advice has hardened to keeping 90% or more of your exposure in real Bitcoin.

item.title: Bitcoin.com News Interviews – Austin Federa: Why Crypto Needs a Faster Internet
item.description:
Is the public internet too slow for the future of finance?


Austin Federa, CEO and co-founder of DoubleZero, joins David Sencil at Korea Blockchain Week 2026 in Seoul to talk about building a dedicated high-performance network for blockchains and markets, and why he thinks connectivity needs the same kind of shift the cloud brought to compute.


Federa explains how DoubleZero Edge delivers traditional-finance-style market data to venues like Hyperliquid, what the SEC no-action letter means for DoubleZero's token and contributors, and why crypto may need a Section 230-style framework so protocols can fight hacks without inheriting liability.


We cover:

  • Why the public internet is a poor fit for time-sensitive financial data
  • DoubleZero's mission to do for connectivity what the cloud did for compute
  • How DoubleZero Edge streams order book data from venues like Hyperliquid
  • Why AI could give everyday traders HFT-grade tools
  • What the SEC no-action letter means for DoubleZero's token
  • Crypto's Section 230 problem: stopping hacks without inheriting liability
  • DoubleZero's token model, burns and the Amazon flywheel


Filmed at Korea Blockchain Week 2026.

Host: David Sencil


Will every trader soon have an HFT firm in their pocket?


🎧 Be sure to subscribe on your favorite podcatcher to catch more conversations with industry leaders, economists, and builders shaping the future of crypto and finance.


Then join our community and follow us for the latest updates ⬇️

item.title: The Bitcoin Infinity Show – Bitcoin Is Antifragile with Tomer Strolight | Bitcoin Infinity Show #222
item.description:
Tomer Strolight joins the Bitcoin Infinity Show to talk about the aftermath of the BIP-110 fork attempt, why he ran Knots but never followed the hard fork off Bitcoin, and what the Cold Card entropy exploit and the Liquid hack revealed about Bitcoin security. He and Knut get into why hard forks are so close to impossible, the hierarchy of principles that should sit above any single policy fight, and whether SegWit and Taproot look like own goals in hindsight. They finish on Bitcoin as antifragile money, why worldwide self-custody adoption may never be necessary, and what to do with the freedom that sound money actually buys you.

item.title: House of Satoshi - Bitcoin und Friends – #66 Die Community fragt, Alexander Thoma antwortet | House of Satoshi x PostFinance:
item.description:
Was ist Bitcoin eigentlich? Klingt banal, doch Alexander Thoma stellt die Frage in jedem Vorstellungsgespräch.


Als Head Digital Assets bei PostFinance verantwortet Alex mit seinem Team das gesamte Krypto-Angebot.


In dieser Episode stellt er sich den Fragen unserer Community. Was dich erwartet:

  • Was Bitcoin wirklich ist und warum das Netzwerk keinen Chef braucht, um sich selbst zu justieren
  • Quantencomputer: Weltuntergang für Bitcoin oder lösbares Problem?
  • Der Bank vertraust du deine Aktien und ETFs an, bei Krypto plötzlich nicht mehr. Warum eigentlich?
  • Die Schweiz kann Banking wie kaum ein anderes Land. Warum hat sie trotzdem keinen grossen Stablecoin?
  • Ist der Bärenmarkt vorbei? Die ehrlichste Antwort, die du von einer Bank hören wirst.


Krypto bei PostFinance: https://www.postfinance.ch/de/privat/anlegen/moeglichkeiten/krypto.html


Das ist eine bezahlte Kollaboration zwischen House of Satoshi und PostFinance.

]]>

item.title: Bitcoin für Frauen – Folge 4: Warum Bitcoin entstand – von der Finanzkrise zur ersten Überweisung
item.description:
Warum gibt es Bitcoin überhaupt? Um das zu verstehen, schauen wir in dieser Folge zurück auf die Finanzkrise von 2008. Was lief damals schief – und warum mussten Banken gerettet werden?

Von dort führt uns die Geschichte zu Satoshi Nakamoto und seiner Idee: digitales Geld, das wir direkt an andere Menschen schicken können, ohne dass eine Bank die Zahlung für uns abwickeln muss.

Aber wie verhindert man, dass digitales Geld einfach kopiert und mehrfach ausgegeben wird? Und was passierte, als Satoshi die ersten zehn Bitcoin an Hal Finney schickte?

Wir gehen diesen Fragen gemeinsam nach – Schritt für Schritt, mit einfachen Beispielen und ohne vorausgesetztes Technikwissen.

Schön, dass du dabei bist! Deine Melly


]]>

item.title: Epicenter - Learn about Crypto, Blockchain, Ethereum, Bitcoin and Distributed Technologies – The DAO Security Fund: Turning a Historic Hack into Ethereum's Future | Griff Green
item.description:
Ten years after The DAO hack changed Ethereum forever, Griff Green returns to Epicenter to discuss the next chapter: the DAO Security Fund.


As a co-initiator of The DAO, Griff shares the untold story of recovering funds after the hack, why over 75,000 ETH remained untouched for years, and how its staking yield is now funding public goods for Ethereum security. The conversation also explores a provocative idea: Ethereum is incredibly secure—but still not safe for everyday users.


Topics covered:

1. The inside story of The DAO and its recovery

2. Why the DAO hack may be the only hack where everyone made money

3. The DAO Security Fund and funding Ethereum security

4. Quadratic funding, grants & public goods

5. Why phishing and UX remain Ethereum's biggest weakness

6. Can Ethereum become safer than traditional banks?

7. The future of safer wallets, OpSec, and the Ethereum Economic Zone


If you enjoyed the episode, don't forget to subscribe for more conversations with the builders, founders and investors shaping the future of crypto.

item.description:
Aaron and Sjors discuss the COLDCARD hack: the bug itself, how it could have happened, and some reflections on having had Coinkite as a sponsor.

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – The AI Crisis
item.description:
In this Take, I break down why the biggest AI labs, while deeply unprofitable sitting on massive future compute obligations, are racing toward trillion-dollar valuations. I explore how open-source competition, especially from China, is crushing their moat, and why that pushes them toward lobbying for fear-driven regulation, immunity, and government partnerships. Ultimately, I argue that the AI panic is about preserving a failing business model and building a centralized surveillance infrastructure, and why we shouldn’t be the ones paying their bill.

Chapters

(00:00:00) - Introduction

(00:00:27) - OpenAI’s insane obligations

(00:01:51) - Anthropic’s profit illusion

(00:02:40) - Trillion-dollar IPO dreams

(00:03:12) - The open-source threat

(00:04:38) - Engineering the panic

(00:06:10) - Regulatory moat and control

(00:09:11) - What this is all about

item.title: Krypto Corner – Bitcoin, ETF und NFT: Sicher investieren - Krypto verstehen und sicher starten – Kapitel 15 Warnung vor der Parkplatz-Falle: Krypto-Steuern in DE! | Podcast: Krypto Corner
item.description:
Hör auf, völlig isoliert auf rote oder grüne Kerzen-Charts zu starren! Der wahre Zustand des Krypto-Marktes zeigt sich erst, wenn du die echte Bewegung der Liquidität verstehst. In dieser extrem atmosphärischen und lehrreichen Episode der Krypto Corner sitzen wir mit unserer Berliner WG in einem Kreuzberger Späti und sezieren die sogenannten "Netflows".

Sophie und Max erklären genial einfach, warum große Krypto-Börsen wie Coinbase oder Binance im Grunde wie gigantische Stauseen funktionieren. Fließen Bitcoins in rauen Mengen von diesen Börsen ab (Outflow), trocknet das Angebot aus – ein massives bullishes Signal. Fließen sie jedoch in Panik zurück auf die Börse (Inflow), öffnen sich die Schleusen für den Abverkauf. Zudem klären wir die Rolle von Funding Rates und Stablecoins, die als "trockenes Schießpulver" an der Seitenlinie auf ihren massiven Einsatz warten.

Doch diese Stablecoins bergen eine extrem dunkle Seite! Im absolut kritischen Steuer-Deep-Dive dieser Folge warnen wir vor der "Parkplatz-Falle". Unzählige Einsteiger flüchten vor einem drohenden Crash panisch aus Bitcoin in USDC oder Tether, in dem tödlichen Irrglauben, so lange keine Steuern zu zahlen, bis sie am Ende in echte Euro auszahlen. Wir erklären dir brutal ehrlich, warum genau dieser Denkfehler dich in Deutschland in den Ruin treiben kann und wie du die komplexen Tausch-Regeln in Österreich sicher navigierst.

In dieser Folge erfährst du: • Warum du den Krypto-Markt ab heute wie ein gigantisches hydraulisches System betrachten musst. • Wie du "Exchange Netflows" (Zuflüsse und Abflüsse) als extrem wertvolles On-Chain-Kaufsignal nutzt. • Warum eine hohe "Stablecoin Dominance" auf den Börsen wie explosiver Treibstoff wirkt. • Die "Parkplatz-Falle": Warum die Flucht in Stablecoins in DE ein sofortiger, voll steuerpflichtiger Verkauf ist! • Warum du in Deutschland im schlimmsten Fall hohe Steuern für Krypto-Geld zahlen musst, das du auf der Börse danach komplett verloren hast.

Diese Episode basiert auf Kapitel 15 des Einsteiger-Romans „Krypto verstehen – sicher starten. Band 1“ von Sascha Swen Heiter. Verantwortung steht über Spekulation. Beobachte die Flüsse, halte dein Pulver trocken, tappe nicht in die Steuerfalle und investiere mit Köpfchen!

📚 Das Buch zur Show: Wenn du das gesamte Wissen sofort anwenden möchtest – von der Einrichtung deiner Hardware Wallets über die Nutzung von Burner Wallets bis hin zu wichtigen rechtlichen und steuerlichen Themen in der DACH-Region – hol dir das komplette Buch! 👉 https://amzn.eu/d/06DuLLUw

🔗 FOLGE MIR FÜR MEHR KRYPTO-WISSEN: • Spotify:https://open.spotify.com/show/5MOMwCZpWNvm6J52jkdLcl?si=yq7YoMyZSnWCg_xrVLcnww • Apple Podcasts:https://podcasts.apple.com/de/podcast/krypto-corner-bitcoin-etf-und-nft-sicher-investieren/id1872914214 • Instagram:https://instagram.com/Swen_Heiter

⚖️ Rechtliche Hinweise / Haftungsausschluss: Die in diesem Podcast geteilten Inhalte dienen ausschließlich der allgemeinen Information sowie der Unterhaltung und stellen keine Anlage-, Rechts- oder Steuerberatung dar. Investitionen in Kryptowährungen sind hochriskant und können zu einem Totalverlust des eingesetzten Kapitals führen. Jeder Hörer und Zuschauer handelt absolut eigenverantwortlich. Besonders bei steuerlichen Themen ist zu beachten, dass die steuerliche Behandlung von Kryptowährungen sehr komplex ist. Bitte konsultiere für die aktuell geltende Rechtslage in der DACH-Region zwingend einen qualifizierten Steuerberater. item.title: Should I Invest in Bitcoin? Grow Your Wealth & Understand the Cryptocurrency Bit Coin, for Millennials Serious About Money and Investing – Your Bank Balance Is Not Actually Yours Until They Say So - Here Is Why Bitcoin Changes That (Bit Coin, Wealth & Investing)
item.description:
Most Bitcoiners sell self custody like the bank is about to raid you tonight. I started on an exchange, and I would tell you to as well. But there is a line where that changes, and today I am giving you the exact question I use to know when I have crossed it.

  1. What your bank balance actually is, and the real story of what happened in Cyprus in 2013 when a European bank took nearly half of people's savings, completely legally
  2. The word Europe's most senior official was widely reported as using about ten trillion euros of ordinary people's savings last month, and what it actually reveals about how your money is viewed from the top
  3. The one honest question that tells you when you have genuinely outgrown keeping your Bitcoin on an exchange, no panic, no arbitrary amount, just the test I use myself


I built a free calculator that shows exactly what consistent monthly Bitcoin investing could do to your wealth over 5, 10 or 20 years. It's called the Steady Stack Calculator — punch in what you can afford to put in each month and see what the numbers actually look like at the other end. Most people are genuinely surprised. You can also download the 10 Bitcoin Mistakes to Avoid document completely free at the same link.

Steady Stack Calculator and 10 Bitcoin Mistakes Document — click here to grab both for free

Hit follow, so you never miss the latest insights on money, finance, invest and build wealth - plus clear guidance on cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, and Bit Coin for today’s serious investors.


]]>

<p><a href="https://www.trace.com/">Trace Mayer</a> joins Cedric Youngelman on the Bitcoin Matrix Podcast, sharing his origin story from playing text-based online games and experimenting with digital gold currencies in the mid-90s to discovering Bitcoin through deep study of Austrian economics and monetary law in law school. They explore the hidden history of money in American law, the significance of Dr. Edwin Vieira's Pieces of Eight, and how GATA exposed central bank gold price suppression. The conversation digs into Trace's pioneering role in Bitcoin -- from launching Run to Gold in 2008 and funding Kraken and Armory to coining the stock-to-flow concept for Bitcoin -- and his conviction that monetary sovereignty is worth fighting for despite intimidation from those who control the existing financial system.

item.title: The Bitcoin Frontier – Inside Wall Street’s bitcoin playbook with Denny Galindo
item.description:
Denny is a wealth manager and bitcoin research lead at Morgan Stanley, where he bridges traditional finance and bitcoin for high-net-worth investors. He operates inside one of the world’s largest financial institutions while developing frameworks to help advisors understand and allocate to bitcoin.

In this episode, Denny joins The Bitcoin Frontier to share how investors should think about bitcoin in a portfolio, the three core investor buckets driving adoption, and his thoughts on determining whether you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin. We dig into bitcoin’s market cycles and seasonal framework, the role of global money supply in driving returns, and practical strategies for gaining exposure in a volatile asset.

SUPPORT THE PODCAST:
 → Subscribe
 → Leave a review
 → Share the show with your friends and family
 → Send us an email: podcast@unchained.com
 → Learn more about Unchained: https://unchained.com/?utm_source=you...
→ Book a free call with a bitcoin expert: https://unchained.com/consultation?ut...

TIMESTAMPS:
0:00 – Intro & Denny’s role bridging traditional finance and bitcoin
2:00 – From equity research to leading bitcoin insights at Morgan Stanley
4:20 – The three investor buckets: digital gold, venture, and diversifier
7:30 – How institutions evaluate volatility and correlation
10:50 – Where bitcoin fits in portfolios today (risk asset vs store of value)
14:00 – How to determine if you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin
18:00 – Why most investors are still early (0–4% allocation range)
21:40 – Will the three investor frameworks converge over time?
23:10 – Bitcoin cycles: macro liquidity vs halving-driven supply shocks
26:30 – Using cycles for rebalancing vs long-term holding strategies
31:20 – Tail risks: quantum computing and “earthquake” scenarios
36:10 – Bitcoin as a global store of value and M2-driven returns
41:10 – Modeling long-term returns: monetary expansion + adoption
48:30 – How to build a position: dollar-cost averaging and timing
52:15 – Seasons of bitcoin: winter, spring, and portfolio adjustments
55:00 – What it takes for bitcoin to become a standard portfolio allocation

WHERE TO FOLLOW US:

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – The AI Crisis
item.description:
In this Take, I break down why the biggest AI labs, while deeply unprofitable sitting on massive future compute obligations, are racing toward trillion-dollar valuations. I explore how open-source competition, especially from China, is crushing their moat, and why that pushes them toward lobbying for fear-driven regulation, immunity, and government partnerships. Ultimately, I argue that the AI panic is about preserving a failing business model and building a centralized surveillance infrastructure, and why we shouldn’t be the ones paying their bill.

Chapters

(00:00:00) - Introduction

(00:00:27) - OpenAI’s insane obligations

(00:01:51) - Anthropic’s profit illusion

(00:02:40) - Trillion-dollar IPO dreams

(00:03:12) - The open-source threat

(00:04:38) - Engineering the panic

(00:06:10) - Regulatory moat and control

(00:09:11) - What this is all about

item.title: All In Bitcoin – Susie Violet Ward : What Politicians Really Think About Bitcoin I All in Bitcoin w/CK
item.description:
🎙️CK sat down with Susie Violet Ward, co-founder of Bitcoin Policy UK, to find out what politicians really think about Bitcoin when the cameras are off.

Susie takes us behind closed doors in Westminster: how little many policymakers understand about Bitcoin, who really influences regulation, and why money and lobbying can matter more than knowledge.

They discuss Bitcoin vs. crypto, stablecoins and CBDCs, digital ID, institutional adoption, financial surveillance, the future of independent journalism — and what happens when governments realise they can’t stop Bitcoin.

item.title: The Peter McCormack Show – #217 - Lee Cronin - AI Will Never Be Conscious. This Is How We Create Real Life.
item.description:
Chemist and University of Glasgow professor Lee Cronin argues that the current tech narrative is a "massive AI delusion," dismissing modern artificial intelligence as an advanced form of plagiarism rather than a new life form. While Silicon Valley predicts the imminent arrival of sentient machines, Cronin explains that AI models are merely trained on human history-making them powerful tools, but fundamentally incapable of the curiosity, consciousness and biological intelligence that define true life.


Instead of fearing silicon, Cronin’s actual mission is far more ambitious: programming chemistry to solve the origin of life and turn sand into living cells. In this episode, we explore why biological consciousness is tied to an unbroken 3.8-billion-year evolutionary lineage and why silicon will never replicate it. Cronin also breaks down why DNA might just be a cosmic fluke, how chemistry can be used to measure the complexity of life and why he firmly believes we will detect actual alien life within the next two decades.

item.title: 21talk – $500k pro Bitcoin durch US-Großinvestoren? | 21weekly mit Florian Bruce
item.description:
Podcast) über die wichtigsten Entwicklungen und News der vergangenen Woche im Bitcoin Space.Im Fokus steht der neue Gesetzesentwurf zur Krypto-Besteuerung in Deutschland und was ein möglicher Wegfall der einjährigen Haltefrist für Anleger bedeutet. Gleichzeitig werfen wir einen Blick auf die optimistische 500k-Prognose für den US-Markt und ordnen das veränderte institutionelle Narrativ ein.Passend dazu analysieren wir die anhaltenden Rekord-Zuflüsse der Spot-ETFs und das Kaufverhalten institutioneller Investoren bei Korrekturen laut neuester Bitwise-Umfrage. Zudem beleuchten wir den BlackRock-Report zu Bitcoin als Währung für künstliche Intelligenz und gehen auf die aktuelle Debatte rund um Markttrends und den inneren Wert von Bitcoin ein.

item.title: Madelon Praat | Macro-economie, Investeren, Bitcoin en Goud – Box 3 wordt nóg erger: Belasting over winst die je niet hebt gepakt
item.description:
🪙 5 gram gratis zilver bij goud999: https://madelonvos.nl/goud999

🥇 Teken de goud petitie: https://goudinbox3.petities.nl/

💶 Download eindspel ebook: https://madelonvos.nl/eindspel

❤️ Abonneer gratis en klik op de bel voor meer: https://madelonvos.nl/abonneergratis

🤍 Meer van deze content? Like, volg en deel deze podcast via ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Spotify⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ of het platform waar je dit luistert.



Het is chaos. Het nieuwe box 3-stelsel zou eerlijker worden, maar sinds de nieuwe plannen vorige week bekend zijn gemaakt, is de onrust groot: in de politiek én bij spaarders, ondernemers en beleggers.De vermogenswinstbelasting wordt gepresenteerd als een overwinning, terwijl de kleine spaarder en belegger de dupe zijn. Wat minder aandacht krijgt, is dat je over de papieren winst op bitcoin en edelmetaal voorlopig jaarlijks belasting lijkt te moeten betalen, ook als je niets hebt verkocht. We kijken daarom naar de uitvoering en naar mogelijke oplossingen.Ondertussen begeeft de obligatiemarkt zich op dun ijs. Wereldwijd stijgen de rentes tot niveaus die we in jaren niet hebben gezien, en het renteverschil tussen Frankrijk en Duitsland groeit. Wat zegt dat over het vertrouwen van beleggers? En hoeveel ruimte hebben overheden nog als inflatie en grondstoffenschaarste de rente verder opstuwen?Die hogere rente raakt ook de vastgoedmarkt. En schrik niet: Nederlandse huizen kunnen volgend jaar in reële termen in waarde dalen.Vandaag bespreken we drie krachten die bepalen hoeveel er van jouw vermogen overblijft: belasting, rente én inflatie. Daarover meer in deze aflevering van Madelon Praat.


Volg mij voor meer via @madelonvos: https://madelonvos.nl/social-media/

item.title: 21Focus - Der Bitcoin-Unternehmer Podcast – Aus der Banken IT in die Welt von Bitcoin - Harald Betz
item.description:
Folge #61 – Ein Gespräch über Banken IT und Bitcoin Bücher

Harald Beetz ist seit fast 20 Jahren selbstständig in der Beratung für Banken und Rechenzentren. Angefangen als Banklehrling bei der Sparkasse, hat er früh den Wandel von Beratung hin zu reinem Vertrieb erlebt und sich auf IT-Projekte spezialisiert. In diesem Gespräch erzählt er, wie er von der Banken IT zu Bitcoin kam, warum er mit seiner Frau einen Roman über Geld schrieb und wie er sich heute zwischen Beratung und Content rund um Bitcoin positioniert.


Du erfährst,

  • wie Harald die Bankenwelt von innen erlebt hat,
  • welche Herausforderungen und Chancen es als IT-Berater gibt,
  • warum er Bitcoin zunächst wieder verkaufte und später mit völlig anderem Blick neu entdeckte,
  • wie aus einer Buchidee seiner Frau ein gemeinsames Projekt wurde
  • und welche unternehmerischen Lektionen er aus fast zwei Jahrzehnten Selbstständigkeit mitnimmt.


Kapitel:

  • 00:00 Begrüßung und Vorstellung
  • 02:15 Vom Banklehrling zum IT-Berater
  • 07:40 Veränderungen in der Bankenwelt seit den 2000er Jahren
  • 15:10 Einstieg in die Selbstständigkeit und erste Projekte
  • 22:05 Gescheiterte Produktidee und der Wechsel zur Beratung
  • 29:15 Erster Kontakt mit Bitcoin und die zweite Begegnung
  • 36:50 Der Roman über Geld und Bitcoin
  • 44:20 Zukunft der Beratung im Banken- und Bitcoin-Umfeld
  • 49:00 Wichtigste Tipps für Vertrieb und Resilienz


Links:

Youtube: youtube.com/@MiesesGeld

Webseite: miesesgeld.de

LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/haraldbetz


---

Hallo, mein Name ist Daniel Wingen und ich suche den Austausch mit anderen Unternehmern die in Bitcoin eine wichtiges Werkzeug für ihr Unternehmen sehen. Ich möchte selbst lernen und andere dazu inspirieren sich mit Bitcoin im eigenen Unternehmen zu beschäftigen.

item.title: Nerd Culture • A Gamekings Podcast – #278 over Resident Evil en campy 80's horror films
item.description:
Nerd Culture #278 is ook te bekijken via https://youtu.be/eDMrPF2_hms

In Nerd Culture 278 schuift speciale gast Skate aan bij Koos voor een aflevering die diep de krochten van de horrorfilm induikt. Van de campy horror uit de jaren 80 tot obscure cultfilms waar de gemiddelde bioscoopbezoeker waarschijnlijk nog nooit van heeft gehoord: The Entity, Fire in the Sky, Xtro, Re-Animator, Videodrome, Sundel Bolong en Mystics in Bali komen allemaal voorbij. Ook blikken we nog even terug op Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil, ditmaal mét spoilers. Pasted markdown

Daarna is het tijd voor het laatste nerdnieuws. We bekijken de trailer van Robert Eggers’ Werwulf, bespreken Mike Flanagans poging om The Exorcist nieuw leven in te blazen en staan stil bij het vertrek van David Fincher bij Netflix. Verder komen onder andere Guillermo del Toro’s frustraties met videogameverfilmingen voorbij.

Nieuwe Skywalker trilogie voor Star Wars

Ook lijkt de toekomst van Star Wars langzaam vorm te krijgen. Jon Watts, regisseur van de Tom Holland Spider-Man-trilogie en mede-bedenker van Skeleton Crew, is in beeld om de eerste film van Simon Kinbergs nieuwe Star Wars-trilogie te regisseren. Die trilogie zou verdergaan waar de Skywalker Saga na Episode IX stopte, met Daisy Ridleys Rey opnieuw in een rol. Daarmee zou Watts feitelijk Episode X voor zijn rekening nemen. Het project is nog niet officieel groen licht gegeven door Disney, maar zou na Starfighter momenteel het verst gevorderde Star Wars-filmproject zijn.

David Fincher stopt met Netflix

Na een samenwerking van ruim tien jaar komt er een einde aan de exclusieve deal tussen David Fincher en Netflix. De regisseur kiest ervoor zijn contract, dat volgend jaar afloopt, niet te verlengen. Fincher was vanaf House of Cards nauw betrokken bij de streamer en maakte er onder meer Mindhunter, Mank, The Killer en The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Een definitieve breuk hoeft het overigens niet te zijn: toekomstige samenwerkingen met Netflix blijven mogelijk.

Wil je adverteren bij de podcast Nerd Culture óf misschien bij een andere podcast van ILVY Network? Mail dan naar management@ilvy.com en/of kijk even op de website: https://ilvy.com/podcast

See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

]]>

item.title: Over The Horizon: A Bitcoin Podcast – How STRC and Digital Credit Could Break the Four-Year Bitcoin Cycle with Jeff Walton
item.description:
In this episode, Jeff Walton, Chief Risk Officer at Strive, joins me to break down why Bitcoin may have already bottomed and why the market structure around it is changing faster than most people realize.

We cover:

• Why Jeff believes Bitcoin’s four-year cycle may be over

• How digital credit instruments like STRC are changing Bitcoin capital flows

• Why Strategy’s preferred equity products could pressure traditional credit markets

• The difference between transparent digital credit and opaque private credit

• How AI is reshaping productivity, work, and the K-shaped economy

• Why asset-backed credit may matter more in an AI-driven world

• The biggest regulatory hurdle facing Bitcoin adoption by banks

• How Bitcoin-backed capital markets could evolve from here

Jeff also shares how he personally uses AI, the business models he thinks are hiding in plain sight, and why Bitcoin-based credit instruments may be far earlier than most people think.

item.title: POD256 | Bitcoin Mining, Freedom Tech, and Awesome Tangents – 127. Self-Hosted AI and Open Mining: Tools for a More Sovereign Future
item.description:
In this episode, we recapped Tyler’s trip to the Midwest Bitcoin Summit in Columbus and dug into a theme that kept surfacing throughout the week: how patents and closed systems can slow adoption, while open-source development unlocks entirely new markets. We connected historical examples like automated flour mills, steam engines, and aluminum production to the current state of Bitcoin mining, where a small number of hardware vendors still hold too much of the stack behind closed doors. We talked through why open hardware and software matter so much for Bitcoin’s resilience, how centralization creates both censorship and supply-chain risk, and why we believe the economic incentives will ultimately favor open designs, shared reference implementations, and broader participation across the mining ecosystem.

We also spent time on the rapid rise of self-hosted AI and how it is already becoming a force multiplier for open-source builders. We shared experience setting up a private local LLM on a new Mac Mini, and we explored how AI agents can help with hardware design, software development, pull request review, and even activist tools built at a recent AI Hack for Freedom event. From LibreBoard progress and Adit boards to new Bitaxe enclosures, Proto development, and WhatsMiner-based community builds, this conversation tied together the bigger picture: open tools, sovereign infrastructure, and the growing set of building blocks that can make Bitcoin mining more accessible, decentralized, and unstoppable.

]]>

item.title: The Daily Source Code 863 Bitcoin F.U.B.A.R. Friday – Epic Podcast ~The Daily Source Code 863 Bitcoin F.U.B.A.R. Friday
Natalie Brunell's Coin Stories – Paula Pendley: Major Victory for Bitcoin
item.description:
My guest this week is Paula Pendley, a partner at Nelson Mullins who defends data centers and Bitcoin miners in court, and she joins us as the fight over where these facilities get built is spreading across the country. Towns are passing moratoriums, politicians are campaigning on power bills, and the coverage so far has mostly come from one direction.

item.title: Thank God for Bitcoin – TGFB Episode 83: A Candid Conversation with Rapper and Truth-Teller, Zuby
item.description:
Zuby (@ZubyMusic) joins Jordan Bush for a wide-ranging conversation about faith, courage, and what it takes to be a positive voice in a divided world. He tells the story of his path from independent rapper to one of today's most recognizable social commentators, and how the COVID era pushed him to start speaking out. He also reflects on the upbringing that shaped his character.

From there, Zuby and Jordan dig into the ideologies shaping public discourse: gender norms, privilege, victim mentality, and the grievance culture that keeps people divided. Zuby makes the case for empowerment over resentment, for solutions over complaints, and for a sturdier definition of love and care. He closes by sharing how his faith has grown, why he worries about the UK's loss of national pride and purpose, and why he still believes optimism and individual responsibility can change things.

Rapper. Author. Speaker. Coach. Host @ZubyPodcast

'Strong Advice' book https://zubymusic.gumroad.com/l/zubyfitness

]]>

item.description:

In this episode: Bitcoin pushes back toward the mid-$80,000s as ETF inflows accelerate, while stress continues to build in the supposedly “safe” parts of the financial system. We look at the 10-year Treasury above 5%, Japan raising rates while the yen weakens, tightening global diesel supplies, Strategy buying Bitcoin again, Sequans exiting its Bitcoin treasury, and the continued migration of traditional finance onto digital rails. item.title: Bitcoin Rails | Isabel Foxen Duke – PIPEs, Witness Encryption & the Future of Privacy on Bitcoin | MISHA & CLARA
item.description:
Isabel Foxen Duke sits down with [[alloc] init] co-founder Misha Komarov and Head of Protocol Research Clara Shikhelman to examine PIPEs, a cryptographic framework that utilizes witness encryption—a primitive long dismissed as purely theoretical—to unlock advanced Bitcoin programming without a soft fork.

Breaking away from consensus bottlenecks, PIPEs aims to emulate native Bitcoin covenants and enable fully trustless, pessimistic single-transaction proofs. The episode unpacks the technical evolution from functional encryption to witness encryption in PIPEs v2, detailing how executing a specific computation correctly can cryptographically unlock a signature.

Although the underlying cryptographic assumptions remain experimental and unhardened, Komarov and Shikhelman believe PIPEs could potentially render optimistic bridges obsolete.

This episode of Bitcoin Rails is brought to you by:

LayerTwo Labs — developing research, software, and technologies for scaling Bitcoin via the integration of Drivechains (BIP 300/301)

Hashi on Sui Network — a primitive for executing Bitcoin DeFi transactions, without having to trust a federated bridge or other centralized entity

BitBox — an open-source Bitcoin-only hardware wallet, with smooth UX and no compromises on security. Check out Bitbox [dot] swiss and use code BITCOINRAILS to get a discount

TIMESTAMPS:

🎙️ 01:42 Tying PIPEs to the mission at [[alloc] init]

🔓 08:31 Defining witness encryption and conditional decryption

🛠️ 23:59 Shifting from functional encryption (PIPEs v1) to witness encryption

📜 26:17 Outlining pre-covenants vs. post-covenants on Bitcoin

🏎️ 39:37 Why PIPEs v2 is far from the end of the road

🌐 56:57 Building meta-protocols and avoiding external sequencer risks

👀 1:05:00 Implementing optional compliant privacy via viewing keys

⚡ 1:15:33 Comparing PIPEs to BitVM and rendering BIPs obsolete

🎲 1:23:07 Evaluating the min-rank hardness assumption

]]>
